title: Leaving a kind note where someone will find it
description: A note costs nothing, takes two minutes, and is found at exactly the moment it is needed: inside a lunchbox, on a colleague's desk, tucked into a returned book.

body.heading: Found, not sent
paragraphs: A spoken compliment evaporates; a note waits. That is its whole magic. The note you leave in the morning is discovered at the tired moment of someone else's afternoon, and it can be re-read — most kind notes are read at least twice, the second time more slowly.
Keep it short and specific. 'Your soup got me through last week' beats a paragraph of general praise, because specifics prove the kindness was noticed, not performed.

body.heading: Where notes land best
paragraphs: Good hiding places are private, not public: inside a coat pocket, on a pillow, in the book someone is halfway through. A note is a gift for one reader, not a display for an audience — never post a photograph of one you wrote.
Sign it or do not; both work. Anonymous notes sparkle with mystery, signed notes strengthen a friendship. The only wrong version is the note never left.

takeaway: Leave short, specific kind notes where one person will find them privately — they are re-read, kept, and cost nothing but two minutes.
